newsitem.title: ITALY: German's Hax says early Italy EMU entry unlikely.
newsitem.headline: German's Hax says early Italy EMU entry unlikely.

text.p: Italy has only a 10 to 20 percent chance of being in the first wave of single European currency members, senior German economist Herbert Hax said in an Italian newspaper interview on Friday.
Hax, an economic councillor to Chancellor Helmut Kohl and chairman of the council of economic advisors known as the "Five Wise Men", was talking to the Turin daily La Stampa.
"Those who know the figures can judge how probable it is that Italy will respect the (Maastricht) criteria," he said, putting this at "between 10 and 20 percent."
He said there were no German or central bankers' plans to delay Italy's membership, "but there is the Maastricht Treaty."

He said that if Italy satisfied all the criteria then clearly it would be a founding member, adding that he did not believe that the countries with strong currencies had a real interest in delaying Italy's membership.
"Today Italy and Spain are a long way from respecting the criteria. If such a country was allowed in, the markets would see this as a signal that the single currency will be weak," Hax said.
